answer_text:
We need

\[
A=n^{3}+12n^{2}+15n+180\equiv 0 \pmod{23}.
\]

Since

\[
180\equiv 19 \pmod{23},
\]

it is enough to study

\[
f(n)=n^{3}+12n^{2}+15n+19 \pmod{23}.
\]

Check \(n=10\):

\[
f(10)=1000+1200+150+19=2369=23\cdot 103,
\]

so \(f(10)\equiv 0\pmod{23}\). Hence \(n-10\) is a factor modulo \(23\). Factoring,

\[
f(n)\equiv (n-10)(n^{2}+22n+5)\pmod{23}.
\]

Now factor the quadratic modulo \(23\):

\[
n^{2}+22n+5\equiv n^{2}-n+5\pmod{23}.
\]

Also,

\[
(n-11)(n-13)=n^{2}-24n+143\equiv n^{2}+22n+5\pmod{23}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
f(n)\equiv (n-10)(n-11)(n-13)\pmod{23}.
\]

So \(A\) is divisible by \(23\) iff

\[
n\equiv 10,\;11,\;\text{or }13 \pmod{23}.
\]

The smallest natural number in these residue classes is \(10\). Indeed,

\[
A(10)=1000+1200+150+180=2530=23\cdot 110.
\]

Thus the smallest natural \(n\) is

\[
\boxed{10}.
\]
